https://atomicdata.dev/properties/descri:
Proposed changes to resources. A Draft is a fork of another resource: it carries the same classes as the resource it forked, alongside the Draft class, and names its original through `originalSubject`. Merging a Draft writes its state onto the original as an ordinary commit signed by whoever holds write rights there, so a Draft needs no special authorization. Drafts and suggestions are the same mechanism: a draft is a fork you merge yourself, a suggestion is a fork you ask someone else to merge.

Note that publication is *not* modelled here. Whether a resource is public is decided by where it lives — a resource in a publicly readable folder is public, one outside it is not. Publishing and archiving are moves, not status changes.

A proposed change to another resource. Added *alongside* the classes of the resource it forked (e.g. `isA: [BlogPost, Draft]`), so the normal views render it. A Draft is an ordinary resource with its own subject, history and rights: it can be edited, discussed and shared like anything else, and it is private exactly when its parent is.
The resource that this Draft proposes to change — the resource it was forked from. Merging the Draft writes its state onto this subject.

The content properties of the original at the moment this Draft was forked, as a JSON object keyed by property URL. Merging diffs the Draft against this base so only the properties the Draft actually changed are written onto the original — a property the Draft left untouched does not revert a concurrent edit to the original. A self-contained base: it needs no retained commit history to reconstruct the forked-from version.

For a Draft of a resource with a Loro-backed body (a document, a canvas), the original's Loro version vector at the moment of the fork, base64-encoded. Merging exports the Draft's body operations since this point and imports them into the original, so the two bodies merge as a CRDT — concurrent edits on both sides are preserved, not overwritten.
